effects: Exactly `assets` USDC is pulled from the signer into the vault by safeTransferFrom (VaultV2.enter).
Vault shares (hyperUSDCa) are minted to `onBehalf`. The number is computed at run time by previewDeposit after accrueInterest.
The deposited USDC is then passed on to the liquidity adapter. This moves no further assets of the signer.
formats.shown: Deposit <assets> USDC for <onBehalf>, with the share ticker hyperUSDCa and the share recipient as fields.

findings.title: deposit: the number of shares minted to onBehalf is not shown; the contract computes it at run time.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.deposit: `uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets);` uses the share price from storage and the adapters. The descriptor has only a 'Share ticker' constant field and no share amount. Case 0 minted 0.01 hyperUSDCa to 0xdead (signer null).
findings.fix: None possible in calldata. The function has no min-shares parameter.

findings.title: deposit: the 'Share ticker' raw constant field adds a line but no amount.
findings.evidence: descriptor deposit field {label:'Share ticker', format:'raw', value:'$.metadata.constants.vaultTicker'} renders as 'hyperUSDCa'.
findings.fix: Optionally fold it into the label, e.g. 'Receive hyperUSDCa shares at', or the intent 'Deposit USDC for hyperUSDCa shares'.

cases.notes: 0.01 USDC out to the vault is shown exactly. Shares went to 0xdead (signer null), and the reader saw that correctly.

effects: USDC is pulled from the signer into the vault. The amount is previewMint(shares), rounded up and computed at run time from the share price.
Exactly `shares` hyperUSDCa vault shares are minted to `onBehalf`.
The pulled USDC is then allocated to the liquidity adapter. This moves no further assets of the signer.
formats.shown: Mint <shares> hyperUSDCa for <onBehalf>. A field names USDC as the deposit asset but gives no amount.

findings.title: mint: the intent 'Mint' never says USDC leaves the signer's wallet to pay for the shares.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.enter: `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets);`. The descriptor has intent 'Mint' and interpolatedIntent 'Mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}'. In case 1 the signer sent 0.999942 USDC out, and the reader had to guess 'likely about 0.99 USDC'.
findings.fix: Use intent 'Deposit USDC for shares' and interpolatedIntent 'Pay USDC to mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}'.

findings.title: mint: the USDC amount spent is computed from the share price and cannot be shown.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.mint: `uint256 assets = previewMint(shares);` comes from storage and adapter realAssets. The function has no max-assets parameter. In case 1 the 0.999942 USDC out is not on the screen; only the ticker 'USDC' is.
findings.fix: None in calldata. Optionally label the field 'Pay with (amount set by share price)'.

cases.notes: The USDC asset is named but the amount (0.999942) is not shown, because the contract computes it. The 0.99 shares went to 0xdead (signer null).

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Exactly `assets` USDC is sent from the vault to `receiver` (VaultV2.exit safeTransfer).
Shares of `onBehalf` are burned. The number is previewWithdraw(assets), rounded up and computed at run time.
When the signer is not `onBehalf`, the signer spends onBehalf's share allowance by that number of shares.
The liquidity adapter may be deallocated to fund the withdrawal. This is internal to the vault.
formats.shown: Withdraw exactly <assets> USDC to <receiver>, with <onBehalf> shown as the owner.

findings.title: withdraw: the number of hyperUSDCa shares burned from the owner is not shown; it is computed at run time.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.withdraw: `uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets);` then deleteShares(onBehalf, shares). In case 2 the signer lost 1997.594375513270424838 hyperUSDCa, which is not on the screen. The function has no max-shares parameter.
findings.fix: None in calldata. Optionally add to the intent that vault shares of the owner are burned, e.g. 'Withdraw {#.assets} to {#.receiver} by burning shares of {#.onBehalf}'.

cases.notes: 2000 USDC in is shown exactly. The 1997.59 hyperUSDCa burned is not shown; the reader guessed that shares were redeemed but had no amount.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Exactly `shares` hyperUSDCa are burned from `onBehalf`. When the signer is not onBehalf, the signer spends onBehalf's share allowance.
USDC is sent from the vault to `receiver`. The amount is previewRedeem(shares), rounded down and computed at run time.
formats.shown: Redeem <shares> hyperUSDCa to <receiver>, with the owner shown. The asset paid out is never named.

findings.title: redeem: the screen never names USDC as the asset paid to the receiver.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.exit: `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets);` sends USDC. The descriptor redeem fields are only shares, receiver and onBehalf, while mint carries an 'underlyingTicker' constant field. In case 3 the signer received 16.507419 USDC, and the reader said 'probably USDC, but the screen doesn't confirm it'.
findings.fix: Add a field {label:'Receive asset', format:'raw', value:'$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker'}. Make the intent 'Redeem {#.shares} for USDC to {#.receiver}'.

findings.title: redeem: 'Redeem {shares} to {receiver}' reads as if the shares go to the receiver.
findings.evidence: interpolatedIntent 'Redeem {#.shares} to {#.receiver}' rendered as 'Redeem 16.498139183621848662 hyperUSDCa to 0x0eBa…'. Per VaultV2.exit, the shares are burned and USDC goes to the receiver.

findings.title: redeem: the USDC amount received is computed at run time and has no minimum bound.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.redeem: `uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares);`. The function has no min-assets parameter. The 16.507419 USDC received in case 3 is not shown.

cases.notes: The 16.498 hyperUSDCa burned is shown exactly. The USDC received (16.507419) is shown with neither asset nor amount; the reader guessed USDC.
